name: Kalimpong
tagline: Monasteries, nurseries and quiet forest villages above the Teesta
summary: Kalimpong is a hill district of West Bengal, east of the Teesta, built around a market town at 1,250 m and a ring of forest villages such as Lava, Rishop, Lolegaon and Sillery Gaon. Go for monasteries, flower nurseries, Kanchenjunga views and red panda forest at a slower pace and lower cost than Darjeeling. October to May is the best time.
meta_description: Plan Kalimpong, Lava, Rishop, Lolegaon and Sillery Gaon: best months, honest costs, routes from Siliguri, homestays and Neora Valley tips.
intro: Kalimpong sits on a ridge between two hills, Deolo and Durpin, about 70 km from Siliguri. The Teesta runs far below and separates it from Sikkim. The town grew as a trading post on the mule route to Lhasa over Jelep La, and the old bazaar, mission schools and Tibetan monasteries still show that past. It became its own district in 2017, carved out of Darjeeling district.

Most visitors spend one or two nights in town, then move out to the villages. Lava, at about 2,195 m, is the gateway to Neora Valley National Park. Rishop sits higher still, at about 2,590 m, with a wide view of the Kanchenjunga range at sunrise. Lolegaon has an old forest and a canopy walk. Sillery Gaon, above Pedong, looks down on the bends of the Teesta.

The district suits travellers who want quiet. There are no toy trains or big malls, and the villages run on homestays where the family cooks for you. Roads are narrow and slow, so plan on 30–40 km an hour. In winter Lava and Rishop can get frost and the odd dusting of snow. In the monsoon, landslides on NH10 and the village roads are common.

Costs are lower than Darjeeling or Gangtok. A village homestay with all meals costs around ₹1,500–2,200 a person, and a shared jeep from Siliguri around ₹200–250 a seat. If you want comfort, a few heritage buildings in town, such as Morgan House and the old Himalayan Hotel, offer rooms with history attached.

highlights.title: Zang Dhok Palri on Durpin Hill
highlights.text: A Nyingma monastery founded by Dudjom Rinpoche, consecrated by the Dalai Lama in 1976, with views over the Relli and Teesta valleys.

highlights.title: Red panda forest in Neora Valley
highlights.text: One of the least disturbed forests in West Bengal, entered from Lava between mid-September and mid-June.

highlights.title: Sunrise from Tiffin Dara above Rishop
highlights.text: A short climb from Rishop gives a wide view of the Kanchenjunga range when the sky is clear.

highlights.title: Lolegaon canopy walk
highlights.text: A hanging walkway through old oak and cypress forest, a few minutes from the village.

highlights.title: The Teesta bends from Ramitey Dara
highlights.text: From the ridge above Sillery Gaon the river twists through the valley in a long series of turns.

highlights.title: Nurseries, cheese and the haat
highlights.text: Cactus and orchid nurseries, local cheese and the Wednesday and Saturday haat give the town its own character.

people: The Lepchas are the oldest people of these hills, and their language and Damsang story are still alive in villages around Pedong and Lolegaon. Most people today are Nepali-speaking Gorkhas from many communities, including Rai, Limbu, Tamang, Gurung, Sherpa, Chettri and Newar. Bhutia and Tibetan families, many of whom came after 1959, keep the monasteries going, and there are old Bengali, Anglo-Indian and Christian communities linked to the mission schools. Hinduism, Buddhism and Christianity sit side by side. Greet people with namaste or a nod, ask before photographing anyone, and remove shoes in monasteries and temples.

months.weather: Cold and mostly clear, 3–15°C in Kalimpong, below zero at night in Lava
months.summary: Clear mornings give good mountain views, and Lava and Rishop sometimes see light snow. Homestays are quiet and some reduce rates.
months.tip: Ask your homestay whether rooms have heaters or extra quilts before you book.

months.weather: Cold, dry and clear, 5–17°C in town
months.summary: A good month for views and for Losar in Tibetan Buddhist homes and monasteries when it falls in February. Nights are still cold in the higher villages.
months.tip: Check the Losar date, which follows the Tibetan calendar and moves each year.

months.weather: Mild days, 9–21°C in town, haze building
months.summary: Rhododendrons start to flower in the higher forest around Lava and Neora Valley. Haze can hide the peaks after mid-morning.
months.tip: Go to viewpoints at sunrise, before the haze rises.

months.weather: Warm days, 13–24°C in town, cool nights in the villages
months.summary: One of the best months for birding and rhododendrons in Neora Valley. Nurseries in Kalimpong are full of flowering plants.
months.tip: Book Lava and Rishop early for the Bengali New Year holiday in mid-April.

months.summary: School holidays in the plains bring families, and the higher villages stay cool. Pre-monsoon storms start in the afternoons.
months.tip: Plan drives and walks for the morning.

months.summary: Rain sets in by mid-June and Neora Valley National Park closes from about 16 June. Landslides on NH10 and the Lava road begin.
months.tip: Leave a spare day in your plan for road blocks. Check current status before you travel.

months.summary: The wettest stretch of the year. NH10 along the Teesta often closes for hours or days after slides, and views are rare.
months.tip: Avoid unless you have flexible dates; consider the Lava–Gorubathan road as an alternative way down.

months.weather: Heavy rain, 18–24°C, leeches in the forest
months.summary: Similar to July. Neora Valley is closed and village walks are slippery.
months.tip: Carry salt or leech socks if you walk in the forest.

months.weather: Rain easing, 17–24°C, clearer spells late in the month
months.summary: The monsoon fades and Neora Valley usually reopens after mid-September. Dashain often begins at the end of the month or in early October.
months.tip: Book early if your trip overlaps the Durga Puja holidays.

months.summary: The best month for views, with washed skies after the rains. Dashain and Tihar fill the town with family visits, tika and lamps.
months.tip: Puja holidays make October the busiest month; book stays and cars two months ahead.

months.weather: Clear and cool, 9–20°C in town, cold nights
months.summary: Long clear spells make this a strong month for Kanchenjunga sunrises. Tihar sometimes falls in early November.
months.tip: Carry warm layers for sunrise at Tiffin Dara and Ramitey Dara.

months.summary: Quiet and clear, with Christmas celebrated in the mission churches. Lepchas gather at Damsang Fort on 20 December for Gaeboo Achyuk's birthday.
months.tip: Book Christmas and New Year week early; it fills with weekenders from Siliguri and Kolkata.

getting_there: Fly to Bagdogra or take a train to New Jalpaiguri (NJP), then drive about 70 km from Siliguri to Kalimpong in 2.5–3 hours. The road runs through Sevoke and up the Teesta on NH10, then climbs from Teesta Bazaar or Chitre. Shared jeeps (about ₹200–250 a seat) and NBSTC buses leave Siliguri through the day; a reserved car costs about ₹3,000–4,000. In the monsoon NH10 is often blocked by landslides, so the longer route through Malbazar, Gorubathan and Lava (or via Damdim) is the fallback. Check current status before you travel. Lava, Rishop and Lolegaon are reached from Kalimpong via Algarah; Sillery Gaon via Pedong.
permits: No permit is needed to visit Kalimpong district, for Indians or foreigners. Neora Valley National Park needs an entry permit and a local guide, arranged at the forest office in Lava, and it closes from about mid-June to mid-September. If you continue into Sikkim, foreigners need an Inner Line Permit, issued at Rangpo or Melli and online. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Kalimpong?
faqs.a: Allow four to six days. Spend one or two nights in Kalimpong town for Durpin, the nurseries and the haat, then two or three nights in villages such as Lava, Rishop, Lolegaon or Sillery Gaon. Roads are slow, so moving every night is tiring. With only two nights, pick the town and one village close by, such as Sillery Gaon via Pedong.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Kalimpong?
faqs.a: October and November give the clearest mountain views and pleasant days of 13–23°C in town. March to May is good for rhododendrons, birds and escaping the heat of the plains. December to February is cold but often clear. Avoid July and August, when landslides block NH10 and the village roads, and Neora Valley National Park is closed.

faqs.q: How do I get from Siliguri to Kalimpong?
faqs.a: The road is about 70 km and takes 2.5–3 hours via Sevoke and NH10 along the Teesta. Shared jeeps leave from stands near Siliguri Junction and Hill Cart Road for about ₹200–250 a seat, and NBSTC buses are cheaper. A reserved car from NJP or Bagdogra costs about ₹3,000–4,000. Prices are indicative.

It is different rather than better. Kalimpong is smaller, quieter and cheaper, with monasteries, nurseries and easy access to forest villages. Darjeeling has the toy train, tea estates and Tiger Hill, and much bigger crowds. Many travellers do both: they are about 50 km apart, a drive of 2.5–3 hours via Teesta Bazaar.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Kalimpong, Lava or Rishop?
faqs.a: No. Kalimpong district is open to Indian and foreign travellers without a permit. You only need an entry permit and a registered guide to walk inside Neora Valley National Park, arranged at the Lava forest range office. If you cross into Sikkim, foreigners need an Inner Line Permit. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I see snow in Kalimpong?
faqs.a: Kalimpong town almost never gets snow. Lava, at about 2,195 m, and Rishop, at about 2,590 m, get light snow on a few days in some winters, usually between late December and February. It is never guaranteed. For reliable snow, plan a day trip to Tsomgo Lake in East Sikkim instead.

faqs.q: Is Kalimpong safe in the monsoon?
faqs.a: The town itself is safe, but the roads are the problem. Landslides on NH10 along the Teesta can close the main route for hours or days, and village roads to Lolegaon and Sillery Gaon become slippery. Build a spare day into your plan, travel in daylight and ask your driver about road status each morning. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Which village should I choose: Lava, Rishop, Lolegaon or Sillery Gaon?
faqs.a: Pick Rishop for the widest Kanchenjunga sunrise, Lava for Neora Valley and the monastery, Lolegaon for old forest and the canopy walk, and Sillery Gaon for the Teesta view and Lepcha history near Pedong. Lava and Rishop pair well; Sillery Gaon is easier to add to a Kalimpong stay or a Silk Route trip.

faqs.q: How much does a Kalimpong trip cost per day?
faqs.a: On a budget, plan ₹1,800–2,600 per person a day for homestays with meals and shared jeeps. With good hotels and a private car, plan ₹4,000–6,000. Heritage rooms, all meals and a private SUV take it to ₹9,000–15,000. A reserved car for a full day of sightseeing costs about ₹2,500–3,500. All prices are indicative.
